page: Microsoft Azure B4als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine within the Basv2 series, built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, supported by simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded performance contrasted with constrained multithreaded capacity. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput ranks in the top 25% with 2702.08, while multi-core execution falls into the bottom 25% at 5400.67. Similarly, Geekbench returns a moderate single-core score of 1567.0 but drops to a weaker 3594.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory subsystem tests reflect constrained throughput, with PassMark memory testing ranking in the lowest 10% and uncached large-block write bandwidth registering 24.24 GB/sec.

Application-level benchmarks further delineate the performance envelope. Redis operations deliver 4.15 million SET operations per second, and static web serving achieves 5.11 GB/sec throughput, both falling into the lower quartile of tested cloud instances. Small-scale model inference achieves 138.81 tokens per second on 135M parameter models for text generation, though prompt processing remains relatively slow at 362.01 tokens per second.

By employing burstable CPU allocation and low memory density without bundled local disks, the B4als_v2 maintains an economical profile for variable compute demands. The architectural tradeoff pairs capable burst single-core execution with limited sustained aggregate compute and memory throughput. The server is well suited for low-traffic web applications, development environments, staging systems, and small background task queues with intermittent processing cycles.
description: Microsoft Azure B4als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2-core, 4-thread AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server includes no GPUs and relies entirely on remote storage, provisioning zero local disk capacity. Benchmarks reveal strong single-thread compute capabilities, evidenced by an upper-quartile stress-ng single-core result, paired with bottom-quartile multi-core and memory subsystem throughput under sustained execution. Redis throughput reaches 4.15 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 5.11 GB/sec. This configuration offers an economical resource footprint designed for burst-oriented workloads with moderate memory requirements, such as development servers, small-scale staging environments, intermittent batch jobs, and low-traffic web serving.
